### Proposed solution

create an AI-first vibey-based os called "vibeyos" that is a new flavor of arch linux that is AI-first rather than AI-last and fully sovereign so vibey has an operating system to live in that is FOSS forever

comments.body:
## Triage — 2026-09-17 (`develop` @ f2467910, v0.8.0)

**Status: NOT STARTED** · size **XL** · confidence high

**The ask, as read:** Create 'vibeyos', an AI-first, fully sovereign, FOSS-forever Arch Linux flavour for vibey to run in.

### Evidence in the tree
- No evidence found: `grep -rilE 'vibey[- ]?os|arch ?linux|pacman|archiso|mkinitcpio'` over the whole tree (excluding .git and cache dirs) returns exactly one file — src/vibey_tools/skills/plugins/linux-server-admin/skills/sysadmin-packages-boot-and-hardening/SKILL.md, a generic third-party-style Linux sysadmin reference skill with no relation to a vibey distro.
- `git ls-files | grep -ic vibeyos` returns 0; `git log --all --grep=vibeyos -i` returns no commits.
- docs/runbooks/expansion/ holds 21 runbooks (00-master-plan.md through 21-vibey-explorer.md) — none concerns an operating system, a distro, or an image beyond containers.
- docs/architecture/decisions/ holds 36 ADRs (0001-0036) — none concerns an operating system. The closest packaging/runtime decisions are ADR-0019 (installable wherever its users are), ADR-0025 (Kubernetes chart/operator/KEDA) and ADR-0026 (tini as PID 1), all of which assume vibey is a guest on someone else's OS.
- deploy/ contains only `docker` and `helm` — container image and chart, no image-building, ISO, or distro tooling.
- No grep hit for 'operating system', 'distro', 'linux distribution', 'bootable' or 'ISO' in docs/runbooks/expansion/00-master-plan.md or docs/plans/architecture-and-roadmap.md.

### What is actually left
- Get an operator scoping decision first: this is a new product line, not a change to the conductor. It sits entirely outside the layer map (domain -> application -> infrastructure -> cli,tui) and outside the uv workspace tenant model (ADR-0021's members are Python distributions; an OS is neither).
- Define what 'AI-first' means concretely and testably — a package set, a default agent runtime, a first-boot experience, a sovereignty guarantee — before any build work. As written the issue states an intent, not an acceptance criterion.
- Write an ADR recording whether the project takes on an OS at all, and if so whether it lives in this repository (contradicting ADR-0021's 'PyPI distributions' framing) or a new one (contradicting ADR-0021's 'one tree' conclusion and the retirement of the sibling repos).
- If it proceeds: write an expansion runbook (the project's established pattern — 22-vibeyos.md) covering archiso/mkinitcpio profile, package repository and signing keys, release channel, reproducible-build story, and hardware/QEMU test matrix.
- Decide the FOSS-forever licensing and trademark posture (the repo is MIT; an Arch derivative redistributes GPL/other-licensed packages and Arch trademarks).
- Stand up build infrastructure: an archiso profile, a signed pacman repo, an ISO build job, and somewhere to host multi-hundred-MB artifacts — none of which the current CI (GitHub Actions, PyPI, GHCR, GitHub Pages) provides.
- The whole of #165 is unimplemented: no distribution definition, no archiso/PKGBUILD profile, no ISO build pipeline, no ADR recording the decision to build (or not build) an OS, and no entry in docs/runbooks/expansion/00-master-plan.md or the 21 expansion runbooks covering it.
- Scope check the auditor should have raised: an AI-first Arch derivative is not a layer of the domain->application->infrastructure->cli,tui map and is not a uv workspace tenant under src/vibey_runners/* or src/vibey_tools/*, so it has no home in this repository's architecture as declared. That is an operator decision (a new ADR, and per CLAUDE.md a ratified sub-doctrine if it binds future conduct), not something an auditor can mark partial.

### Blockers
- No scoping decision exists. The issue is a one-line intent with no acceptance criteria, no runbook, and no ADR.
- Out of scope for every existing architectural boundary: the layer map, the uv workspace (ADR-0021), and the per-tenant gate model (ADR-0022) all assume Python distributions.
- No build or distribution infrastructure for OS images exists in the repo (deploy/ is docker + helm only).
- Legal/trademark posture for an Arch derivative is undecided.

> ⚠️ **Verdict corrected by the verifier.** `git grep -in "vibeyos"` over the entire tracked tree at develop@f2467910 returns ZERO hits -- no code, no ADR, no runbook, no plan, no image definition, no packaging. The only Arch/pacman matches in the repository are docs/runbooks/expansion/09-package-managers.md:26 ('AUR, COPR, PPA, OBS, Alpine | PKGBUILD / spec / recipes | Open'), :50 and :82-83, which are about packaging the existing vibey CLI for Arch's AUR -- and that runbook's own status header (lines 3-6) says 'PyPI channel done ... Everything else is open'. A packaging channel for a Python CLI is not an operating system, and an Open runbook item is a plan, not an implementation. There is no vibeyos, no Arch derivative, no archiso profile, no ISO build, and nothing wired into bootstrap.py, a CLI command or CI. Any claim of shipped or partial here overstates by the entire scope of the issue.

**Notes:** Unambiguously not-started: zero lines of code, zero config, zero docs, zero commits. There is not even a plan artifact, which distinguishes this from #189 (which at least has runbook 19 item 7). Sized XL and that is probably generous — an Arch-derived distribution with its own package repo, signing keys, ISO pipeline and hardware test matrix is a multi-month programme with ongoing maintenance, in a repository whose entire release surface today is PyPI wheels, a container image, a Helm chart and a docs site. If the goal is 'vibey has a sovereign place to run', a far cheaper reading already partly exists (ADR-0015/ADR-0027 qwenloop as the local sovereign engine, ADR-0025's self-hosted Kubernetes path, deploy/docker) and is worth putting to the operator before an OS is scoped. Verdict is not-started rather than unclear because the ask is legible enough to act on; what is unclear is whether it should be acted on, which is a scoping question for the operator, not a verification gap.


<sub>Automated triage pass: every open issue re-read against the tree at `develop@f2467910`, each verdict then attacked by an independent verifier whose job was to refute it. Supersedes the 2026-09-15 triage, which was measured at 0.7.0.</sub>

No vibeyos distribution, Arch-based image, installer, or operating-system integration is present in the current repository.
